job_title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer - Kubernetes Platform
location: US, CA, Santa Clara, United States of America
section_intro:
It's a unique legacy of innovation fueled by great technology-and amazing people.
The GPU, our invention, serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and sits at the heart of our products and services.

We're looking for a Senior SRE to own and scale the Kubernetes platform that assists NVIDIA's chip design (EDA) workloads.

The clusters you run sit alongside some of the largest EDA compute farms in the industry, spanning multiple on-prem datacenters and multiple public clouds.
When these clusters degrade, chip schedules feel it - which is exactly what makes the reliability work exciting.
section_responsibilities:
Own Kubernetes clusters end-to-end - plan, deliver, upgrade, day-2 operations, and decommission - across on-prem datacenters and managed cloud Kubernetes (e.g.
EKS, GKE, RKE, Red Hat OpenShift, etc.).
Define and implement the multi-cluster lifecycle strategy: version skew policy, patch cadence, node image pipelines, controlled rollouts, and safe upgrade mechanics for clusters that can't simply be drained on demand.
Treat on-prem and CSP Kubernetes as one platform with consistent APIs, policy, and observability - not as two disconnected worlds.
Drive everything through Infrastructure-as-Code, GitOps, and declarative config; manual cluster changes should be an anomaly worth investigating.
Design for failure: explicit fault domains, blast-radius containment between clusters and tenants, progressive delivery, and disciplined change control.
Build end-to-end observability (metrics, logs, traces, events) and push toward data-driven and auto-healing operations that materially reduce human intervention.
Participate in on-call, lead incident response, drive root cause analysis, and publish high-quality RCAs that actually change the system.
Partner with EDA engineering, storage, and network teams to land changes cleanly in a fast-moving environment.
Engage and partner with data center operations to help forecast, design and implement the accurate on-prem and cloud deployments to meet architectural needs.
Interface directly with internal EDA tenants/engineering teams to design and implement operational improvements to increase productivity and provide faster and more reliable outcomes as well as partner with the infrastructure services team to help architect the supporting capabilities for intelligent workload routing, observability, dynamic scaling and resource governance.

Deep, hands-on Kubernetes operations experience - you've run it, not just consumed it.

Production experience with CSP-managed Kubernetes - including its upgrade model, networking and IAM integration, node group lifecycle, and where the managed abstraction stops helping you.

NCP estates are open-source-first and heterogeneous-Cumulus Linux, SONiC, Spectrum-X, DOCA/DPU services, upstream Kubernetes and Prometheus/Grafana-so this role is deliberately tool-agnostic: you will meet each partner on the fabric they actually run rather than on a single proprietary product.
section_responsibilities:

Support Day 1 fabric validation and acceptance: InfiniBand and UFM bring-up, Spectrum-X/RoCE Ethernet configuration, cabling and link-health verification, routing and congestion-control validation, and multi-day, multi-rack burn-in against agreed MTBI and goodput targets.
Minimise the time from cluster handover to first production workload, removing duplicated fabric validation across hardware bring-up, managed-service intake and the partner's own network operations teams.
Drive fabric reliability at fleet scale: telemetry for link flaps, retransmits and congestion, fault detection through to remediation, root-cause analysis of network-induced job failures, and measurable improvement of MTBI and job goodput.

Fleet Reliability & Customer Engagement: Demonstrated ability to measure and improve MTBI and job goodput on large GPU clusters-fault detection, drain and remediation workflows, SLO/error-budget definition and post-incident review-combined with a strong consultative background leading architectural reviews and presenting to executive stakeholders.
section_preferred:

Expertise with DOCA and DPU infrastructure services (e.g.
DOCA DPF) for offloaded networking, security and storage services.
Familiarity with fabric and GPU health telemetry-DCGM and XID diagnostics, link-level and switch counters, node-level health agents, and fleet-wide reliability intelligence.
Knowledge of large-scale training traffic behaviour: collective communication (NCCL) tuning, rail alignment, and diagnosing network-bound performance regressions in distributed training jobs.
Experience delivering multi-tenant network isolation for GPU-as-a-service estates-VRF/VLAN/EVPN segmentation, tenant partitioning and secure fabric handover between tenants.

section_intro:
NVIDIA DGX Cloud is an AI Factory designed to power the next generation of AI and industrial-scale breakthroughs.
As the Distinguished Engineer for Security Architecture, within our Security Engineering organization, you will set the security design bar for an AI factory of hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and then build against it alongside the teams.
This is the founding architecture seat in a new organization.
Security Engineering is a new organization at DGX Cloud, accountable for the security outcome of the platform, and this is the architecture function inside it.
You will define the security design standard for DGX Cloud, a bar that sits above the company floor, and hold it from inside the teams doing the building.
Security here is fleet horizontal and stack vertical, so your scope runs from the hardware root of trust and the hardened baseline, through tenancy and GPU workload isolation, to the services and APIs built on top, across every DGX Cloud engineering organization.
A small team of Principal Engineers will report to you and hold the bar at domain depth.
This is still a hands-on seat, and you stay in the design with them.
You will also serve as DGX Cloud's technical interface into NVIDIA's central security organization.
There is no architecture review board here and no approval queue; the bar holds because the strongest security engineers in the room helped set it and helped ship it.
section_responsibilities:
Set the DGX Cloud Security Bar: Own the security design standard across DGX Cloud (tenancy, GPU workloads, identity, supply chain, and isolation) and make it concrete.
Reference architectures, golden paths, and requirements engineers can actually build against, not a policy library.
Hold the Bar by Building: Embed with engineering teams on real work: join the design, learn the code, help ship the thing rather than grade it afterward.
The posture is not "you did this wrong." It is "here are the considerations we need to meet, I will help, let's go to work." Architect the Security Platform: Drive the multi-year architecture for the common security infrastructure the fleet runs on: hardened baselines and patch SLOs, deploy-time policy and admission control, workload identity, supply-chain provenance through signing and attestation, and detection and response tuned to GPU workloads.
Engineer Classes of Risk Out of Existence: Finding a vulnerability is 4% of the work; building the system where it cannot happen again is the other 96%.
You will attack recurring risk at its architectural root, including offensively against our own designs, and feed what you find back into the paved roads, the baselines, and the detections.
Grow the Principal Engineering Bench: Lead a small team of Principal Engineers who report to you and hold the bar across domains.
Set their technical direction, hire into the gaps, and grow each of them into deeper scope than they arrived with.
Multi-Functional Collaboration: Serve as DGX Cloud's primary technical connection into NVIDIA's central security organization, and partner across platform, production engineering, and network security teams.
We operate horizontally across vertically organized teams, with influence rather than authority.
Communicate Risk Upward: When something is going to ship below the bar, write down the gap and what closing it would take, and put it in front of the executives who hold the risk pen.

The bar holds because gaps become visible and owned.

As a Principal Engineer for Security Architecture, within our Security Engineering organization, you will own a core security domain of the AI factory: the architecture, the paved road that delivers it, and much of the code underneath.
You will hold the security design bar across DGX Cloud from inside the teams doing the building, and this is a founding seat on a new team.
Security Engineering is a new organization at DGX Cloud, accountable for the security outcome of the platform, and Security Architecture is the function inside it that holds the design bar.
Security here is fleet horizontal and stack vertical, so your work will cross every DGX Cloud engineering organization: you will embed with the teams building GPU clusters, control planes, and services, join their designs as a participant rather than an approver, and leave behind systems in which an entire class of risk is no longer possible.
There is no architecture review board here and no approval queue.
You are a senior IC with deep security domain knowledge, and the security bar holds because you helped set it and then helped ship it.
section_responsibilities:
Own a Security Domain End to End: Take architectural ownership of a core domain of DGX Cloud security, from the design through the system running in production.
That could be tenant and GPU workload isolation, workload identity, infrastructure and network, supply-chain provenance, hardened baselines and patching, or deploy-time policy and admission control.
Embed with the Teams Building It: Join the design early, write the code, and help land it.
The posture is not "you did this wrong." It is "here are the considerations we need to meet, I will help, let's go to work." Build Paved Roads, Not Gates: Engineer the secure path into the platform so that it is also the easy path.
You are measured by whether teams take that path by default, not by the number of requirements you have written down.
Engineer Classes of Risk Out of Existence: Finding a vulnerability is 4% of the work; building the system where it cannot happen again is the other 96%.
When teams keep missing the same requirement, the paved road is wrong, and fixing the road is our job rather than theirs.
Threat Model and Attack the Design: Run deep-dive threat models across the substrate, the orchestration layer, and the tenancy boundary, then go after your own designs offensively and feed what you find back into the baselines, the guardrails, and the detections.
Carry the Bar into Execution: Turn the DGX Cloud security bar into reference architectures, requirements, and golden paths teams can build against.
Raise gaps early, in the design, with the work to close them attached.
Multi-Functional Collaboration: Partner with DGX Cloud platform, production engineering, and network security teams, and with NVIDIA's central security organization, to make the secure path real in CI/CD and in the hardware lifecycle.
We operate horizontally across vertically organized teams, with influence rather than authority.
section_requirements:
Security and Infrastructure Engineering: Experience (typically 15+ years) across software engineering, SRE, infrastructure, and security engineering.
You build systemic solutions rather than performing manual operations or "tool administration." Production-Grade Coding: A strong software engineering background with the ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code.
You should be comfortable building and operating production services at scale.
Emerging Technology: You work with what is new rather than waiting for it to settle.
Today that means writing and reviewing AI-generated code at the volume it now arrives, putting AI-assisted analysis to work in your own security engineering, and building for agents that act inside the systems you own.
Tomorrow it will mean something else.
Security Architecture in Practice: Designs you own that actually got built and run, in areas like multi-tenant isolation, identity and access, policy enforcement, vulnerability management, or detection engineering.
You stayed on to operate them.
Threat Modeling and System Design: Proven ability to build threat models for complex distributed systems, identify the architectural gaps rather than only the bugs, and engineer the solutions that close them.
Distributed Systems and Linux Depth: Cloud-native architecture, container orchestration (Kubernetes), and hands-on Linux systems security including kernel-level primitives (eBPF, AppArmor, or SELinux).
Influence Without Authority: Experience landing designs through teams you do not own, in environments where credibility and relationships, not org charts, determine whether the work ships.
Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience) with 15+ yrs of relevant experience.
section_preferred:
HPC/AI Security: Experience securing high-performance computing environments, RDMA-based networks, large GPU fleets, or GPU-specific security challenges.
Cloud-Native Identity and Attestation: Expertise in workload identity frameworks (e.g., SPIFFE/SPIRE), hardware root of trust (TPM/HSM) integration, or confidential computing.
Offensive Depth Turned Defensive: Real exploitation, red team, or security research experience that you have converted into engineering: the controls, guardrails, and detections that closed what you found for good.
Open Source Impact: Notable contributions to security-focused open-source projects or a track record of engineering-focused security research.
